concepts.title: Physical Equilibrium and Phase Transformation
concepts.definition: A state established in physical phase changes or dissolution processes where opposing structural transformations proceed at equal rates in a closed system.
concepts.formula: rate of forward phase change = rate of reverse phase change
concepts.key_idea: Physical systems reach equilibrium when macroscopic properties like pressure or solubility remain constant at a given temperature.

concepts.title: Dynamic Nature of Chemical Equilibrium
concepts.definition: A balanced chemical state where forward and backward reactions continue perpetually at equal rates, maintaining constant species concentrations.
concepts.formula: rate of forward reaction = rate of backward reaction
concepts.key_idea: Chemical equilibrium is dynamic rather than static, proven by isotopic tracer mixing in reversible reactions.
question_patterns: explain the dynamic nature of chemical equilibrium using Haber's process

solution_steps.action: confirm constancy of concentrations using tracer or analytical evidence
solution_steps.explain: Verify that macroscopic concentrations remain constant over time, proving the dynamic yet balanced nature of the equilibrium.

concepts.title: Law of Chemical Equilibrium and Equilibrium Constant Kc
concepts.definition: The principle stating that at fixed temperature, the product of product molar concentrations raised to stoichiometric powers divided by reactant molar concentrations raised to their powers is constant.
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium constant Kc depends only on temperature and the stoichiometry of the balanced chemical equation.

concepts.title: Reaction Quotient Qc and Direction of Reaction

concepts.key_idea: Comparing Qc with Kc determines whether net reaction proceeds forward (Qc < Kc), backward (Qc > Kc), or is at equilibrium (Qc = Kc).

concepts.title: Standard Gibbs Energy Change and Equilibrium Constant

concepts.title: Le Chatelier's Principle and Equilibrium Shifts
concepts.definition: Rule stating that when a system at equilibrium experiences a stress in concentration, pressure, or temperature, it adjusts to counteract that stress.
concepts.formula: Qc < Kc leads to forward shift; Qc > Kc leads to reverse shift
concepts.key_idea: Equilibrium position shifts to relieve imposed stresses from species addition/removal, volume changes, or thermal alterations.

concepts.title: Ionization of Polybasic Acids and Polyacidic Bases
concepts.definition: Acids capable of donating multiple protons ionize in sequential steps with progressively smaller dissociation constants.
concepts.key_idea: Electrostatic forces make removing a positive proton from a negatively charged ion progressively more difficult.

concepts.title: Factors Affecting Acid Strength
concepts.definition: Acid strength is governed primarily by the bond strength and bond polarity of the hydrogen-element bond.
concepts.key_idea: Down a group bond strength dominates, while across a period bond polarity dominates acid strength.
question_patterns: explain the trend of acidic strength of hydrides down group 17

solution_steps.action: evaluate periodic trend
solution_steps.explain: Down a group, atomic radius increases and H-A bond enthalpy decreases, enhancing acid strength.

solution_steps.action: evaluate electronegativity
solution_steps.explain: Across a period, electronegativity difference increases H-A bond polarity, enhancing acid strength.

solution_steps.action: Compare acid strength by combining both factors
solution_steps.explain: For elements in the same period, bond polarity dominates; for elements in the same group, bond strength dominates. Combine both to rank acid strength.
